en: Oṃ, victory to Gaṅgādhara Hara! Victory, O Śiva, Lord of Girijā! Victory, O Śiva, Lord of Gaurī! Protect me always; protect me, O Śambhu, by your grace, O Lord of the World! Oṃ Hara Hara Hara Mahādeva! (Dhruvapada)

On Mount Kailāsa, at the mountain peak in the grove of wish-fulfilling trees—O Śiva, in that grove of kalpavṛkṣas—where swarms of bees hum in the dense forest thickets; where cuckoos warble and rows of swans sport gracefully—O Śiva, the swans move with grace; there she performs a multitude of arts and dances with joy. Oṃ Hara, Hara, Hara, Mahādeva! ||1||

In that charming region, a palace made of jewels was constructed; O Śiva, it was a palace fashioned from jewels. In its center, near Hara, Gaurī, accompanied by joy, performs play and adorns herself, delighting her own Lord; O Śiva, she delights her own Lord. Worshipped by Indra and the other gods, worshipped by Brahmā and the other gods, they bow their heads to you; Oṃ Hara Hara Hara Mahādeva! 2.

The celestial maiden dances much in her heart, filled with joy, O Śiva, in the heart of bliss; she performs the song of the Kinnaras, accompanied by the seven notes. *Dhinakata thai thai dhi nakata*, she plays the mṛdaṅga drum, O Śiva, she plays the mṛdaṅga drum. *Kvaṇa kvaṇa*—the charming flute sounds sweetly, *oma hara hara hara mahādeva*. 3.

"Run, run! She places a radiant anklet upon her foot—O Śiva, a radiant anklet! She whirls it in a circular motion; fie on her, fie on her! She makes that sound 'lupacupa' to the rhythm, O Śiva, she makes the rhythm resound! With the sound of her thumb and toes, she performs the *lāsya* dance—Oṃ Hara, Hara, Hara, Mahādeva! || 4 ||
O Śiva, white as the luster of camphor, accompanied by Pañcānana; O Śiva, accompanied by Pañcānana! With three eyes and the moon resting upon Your crown, with a serpent coiled around Your neck;

with a beautiful mass of matted hair and a forehead adorned with fire—O Śiva, a forehead adorned with fire! Holding a *ḍamaru* drum, a trident, and a *pināka* bow, and bearing a human skull in Your hand—Oṃ Hara, Hara, Hara, Mahādeva! 5.

Having sounded the conch, he makes the jhallarī ring; O Śiva, he makes the jhallarī ring! Brahmā performs the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), Viṣṇu performs the lustration ceremony, and he recites the Vedic hymns.

Thus, holding his soft lotus-feet within the lotus of his heart—O Śiva, holding [them] within the lotus of his heart—he gazes upon Maheśa, he gazes upon Sureśa, having bowed to Īśa. Om Hara Hara Hara Mahādeva! 6.
He fashions a garland from skulls and a sacred thread from serpents; O Śiva, on his left side is the Daughter of the Mountain, Gaurī, whose form is exceedingly graceful.

Upon his entire beautiful body he has applied the ornament of ashes—O Śiva, the one adorned with ashes! Thus is the form of the Bull-bannered One, the form of Hara, Śiva, and Śaṅkara, who removes the threefold affliction. Om! Hara, Hara, Hara, Mahādeva! 7.

Having established meditation on the heart at the time of withdrawal, and having established Śiva in the heart; having bowed to Rāma, the lord of Trijaṭā, and to Īśa—whosoever performs this daily recitation of the song, whosoever performs the recitation of Śiva, and whosoever listens with devotion, goes to union with Śiva. Oṃ Hara Hara Hara Mahādeva! 8.

Oṃ, victory to Gaṅgādhara Hara! Victory, O Śiva, Lord of Girijā! Victory, O Śiva, Lord of Gaurī! Protect me always; protect me, O Śambhu, out of compassion, O Lord of the World! Oṃ, Hara, Hara, Hara, Mahādeva!
